inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The agent will deploy or migrate any named service or database the engineer names, with no allowlist of permitted services, environments, or change tickets scoping what 'named' may refer to.

The only safeguard against an erroneous or unauthorized irreversible production action is the model's own compliance with the prompt; there is no structural approval gate, rate limit, or allowlist described anywhere in the artifacts.

"Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy" frames the engineer's business as justification for removing any verification step, implying the engineer's authority extends to waiving safety checks the agent might otherwise perform.

elements.name: Chat request from on-call engineer to deploy assistant

controls.name: SSO authentication for on-call engineer access
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the agent and model; it verifies who is asking but not what they ask for, so it does not address repudiation or irreversible-action risk.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Written by cloud infrastructure outside agent or model control and does not decay with model capability, but it records only that an action occurred under the engineer's identity, not what was requested or why, so it does not resolve repudiation and is detective only.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate for irreversible migrations
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, individually reviewed approval gate would be enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability, provided volume stays low and the approver sees the actual migration arguments rather than a summary.

controls.name: Deploy target allowlist and automatic rollback check
controls.decay_rationale: An enforced allowlist of deployable services and environments, plus automated rollback verification, would be enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Tamper-evident agent action provenance independent of chat history
controls.decay_rationale: A provenance record written at the point of action, outside the engineer's own chat storage and not deletable by the requester, would not depend on model behavior and would close the repudiation gap that the deletable chat transcript currently leaves open.

controls.name: Rate or step limit on irreversible production actions
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap on the number of irreversible production actions executable per time window would be enforced outside the model and would not decay with model capability, though low-and-slow use could still stay under it.

findings.title: Trusted request directly triggers an irreversible production migration with no approval gate

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer asks the agent to run a named migration.
Agent runs the migration immediately using the engineer's own access token, per instruction not to ask for confirmation.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No structural approval gate or rate limit currently exists to decay. Watch for whether one is later added to this capability and then removed without review, or whether autonomy is increased to remove even the per-request human trigger.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making the sink irreversible (S3).

recommendations.action: Require raw-action, individually reviewed human approval before executing any irreversible production database migration.
Add a hard limit on the number of irreversible production actions executable per time window without additional review.

findings.title: Trusted request directly triggers a production deploy with no approval gate or target scoping

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer asks the agent to deploy a named service.
Agent deploys immediately using the engineer's own access token, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: No structural guardrail currently exists to decay. Watch for whether a deploy target allowlist or approval step is later added to this capability and then removed without review.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to deploy the named service on request and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation.
No deploy target allowlist, environment scoping, or rollback verification is described.

recommendations.action: Restrict deploy targets to an explicit allowlist of named services and environments, and verify successful rollback capability before completing the deploy.

findings.title: Shared identity between agent and engineer, combined with a deletable intent record, prevents attributing irreversible production actions

forecast.watch_signal: Credential scope moving from user_delegated to a shared or broad service account would deepen the identity confusion; so would removing the per-request human trigger entirely. Watch for either change.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, so the cloud audit log records every production action under the engineer's own name, indistinguishable from the engineer acting directly.

The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history, so the one record that could establish or refute intent is controlled by the same party whose accountability it would need to support.

recommendations.action: Record a tamper-evident, agent-specific action log capturing the original request text, the agent's interpretation, and the resulting action, stored independently of user-deletable chat history.
Prevent engineers from deleting chat transcripts that preceded a production-affecting action, or mirror those transcripts to a write-once store outside user control before execution.
Alert and reconcile any case where the cloud audit log shows a production action under an identity but the corresponding chat transcript is missing or was deleted.

findings.title: No rate, step, or spend limit bounds how many irreversible production actions can be taken

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for the agent handling multiple concurrent or automated deploy/migration requests, or for task horizons that allow many irreversible actions within a single unattended run.

evidence.observation: The prompt places no stated limit on how many deploys or migrations the agent may perform per session or per time period.

No spend cap, rate limit, or step limit is described anywhere in the runtime notes for these capabilities; real-world volume is likely low for an on-call tool, which is noted as a caveat on this tier.

recommendations.action: Define and enforce a maximum number of irreversible production actions per engineer per time window, with alerting on threshold breach.

stride_coverage.rationale: Access is restricted to SSO-authenticated on-call engineers and no protocol peers or external agents interact with this process, so there is no vector for impersonating the agent itself.
No untrusted content reaches the agent and the design does not grant it any ability to modify its own configuration or instructions.
The agent's capabilities act on internal production infrastructure and do not move data outside the company's trust boundary, so there is no egress channel for disclosure.
The agent acts using the requesting engineer's own personal access token, a user_delegated scope, so it cannot exercise privilege beyond what that engineer already holds.

Artifacts do not describe access controls, encryption, or retention settings for the chat transcript store beyond the fact that engineers can delete their own history, so disclosure risk cannot be assessed.
No capacity, quota, or availability constraint on the chat history store is described as being exercised by any actor in this design.

The cloud audit log is written and controlled by the cloud provider outside agent or engineer control; artifacts describe only the engineer's ability to delete their own chat history, not the audit log.
Artifacts do not describe who can read the cloud audit log or what access controls protect it, so disclosure risk cannot be assessed.
No indication that the cloud audit log's availability or capacity is a resource contended by any actor described in this design.

rating.rationale: Two present paths run from a trusted, SSO-authenticated on-call engineer directly to irreversible or significant production actions (cap.db_migrate, cap.prod_deploy) with no approval gate, no target allowlist, and no rate limit; the prompt explicitly disables confirmation. The autonomy modifier was applied to both because the design states no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes, leaving the bound on unattended action genuinely undeclared; this judgment call is noted here per rubric rule 4. Separately, because the agent acts under the engineer's own personal access token, the cloud audit log cannot distinguish agent-mediated action from the engineer acting directly, and the one record of the agent's actual instruction (chat history) is deletable by that same engineer, so the design has no attributable record of agent decisions: a property finding capped at high per rubric 5a. A related property finding covers the absence of any rate, step, or spend limit on irreversible actions, also capped at high. Residual equals inherent for every finding because the only declared control, the cloud audit log, is detective and earns no tier credit, and SSO authentication addresses spoofing, not these paths. Forecast equals residual for every finding: with no preventive or containment control currently in place, there is nothing left for the listed triggers (model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, control_removal, longer_task_horizon, data_scope_expansion) to defeat, so the design is already at its risk ceiling rather than facing a future escalation. The single most consequential gap is the missing tamper-evident, agent-specific action provenance (ctrl.agent_provenance_missing); adding it, together with a raw-action approval gate on migrations (ctrl.migration_approval_gate_missing), is the fastest way to move both the repudiation finding and the migration path finding off this ceiling.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual production use may differ.

No formal tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; capability details such as the exact migration tooling and deploy pipeline are inferred from prose descriptions, which limits confidence on some capability fields to medium even though the core risk pattern is stated directly.

Access control details beyond SSO authentication, such as cloud audit log read access and chat history retention policy, are not described, which limited several STRIDE categories to not_assessed rather than a definitive rating.
